title: Round 25 Great Lakes state-frame USGS GNIS source register
scope: All-GNIS starter registers for Wisconsin and Michigan. Every seeded row reproduces one USGS GNIS record screened by exact official name, returned type/state/county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and returned GNIS primary point, and cross-checked on two independent USGS surfaces: the USGS GNIS Geocoder service and the staged-products DomesticNames per-state text files (tools/gnis_extract.py; request .arena-gnis/candidates.json; cumulative candidate extract resources/city-subsurface/gnis-candidates-batch7.json with per-state ZIP SHA-256 values). Timms Hill and Mount Arvon additionally carry Domestic Names per-ID identity checks.

usgsGeocoder.use: Fuzzy candidate discovery only. A candidate was accepted only when Name, Type, State, County, GnisId, Latitude, and Longitude all matched the intended feature. Counties, bays, resorts, flowages, historical places, and same-name records of another class or county were rejected explicitly where relevant.

gnisDomesticNames.use: Second-surface cross-check of every seeded FEATURE_ID (name, class, state, primary county, primary point) and per-ID identity checks for Timms Hill (1575464) and Mount Arvon (1623751), extracted in a GitHub Actions runner by tools/gnis_extract.py (.github/workflows/arena-gnis-fetch.yml). The current text layout carries no elevation columns, so the two high-point elevations cite USGS-published state-highpoint values rather than the text file. The candidate extract file is cumulative across batches 7-8; this register is the frozen batch-8 evidence.

selectionRules: VERIFIED=1 is claimed only for an exact official name, compatible GNIS feature class/type, intended state and returned primary county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and an official point returned by a cited USGS service, reproduced identically on the second USGS surface.

Grouped Geocoder Types map explicitly to stored row classes: Cities & Populated Places to Populated Place, Lakes & Reservoirs to Lake for the accepted named lakes, Streams & Canals to Stream for the accepted river records, and Summit to Summit.
A stored GNIS primary point is never described as a municipal boundary, street-address geocode, generic centroid, shoreline polygon, summit outline, or river centerline.

If exact-name candidates remain indistinguishable, or the state-filtered screen returns no intended feature record, the feature is omitted from that state gazetteer and may appear only as a generalized context corridor.
Statewide frames use explicitly synthetic relief gaussians and generalized corridors; no bundled DEM or surveyed boundary is implied.

wisconsin.title: Wisconsin statewide frame (Great Lakes batch)
wisconsin.frameNote: Great Lakes batch: the Madison capital anchor and the Milwaukee shore pair are balanced with the per-ID Timms Hill high point, the Winnebago/Mendota/Devils Lake set, and two in-state river-mouth records (Wisconsin River, Chippewa River). knownLimitations: Wisconsin and Michigan are starter registers, not statewide GNIS extracts. Each contains 12 deliberately selected identity-safe rows.

The USGS Geocoder is a suggestion service; exact-match screening by name/type/state/county/FEATURE_ID is part of the evidence. Every seeded row was reproduced on the second USGS surface (staged-products DomesticNames text) at the same primary point; the two sources agree to well under a metre at the stored precision.

The current DomesticNames text layout carries no elevation columns, so Timms Hill (1,951 feet) and Mount Arvon (1,979 feet) elevations cite USGS-published state-highpoint values; GNIS identity for both rests on the per-ID class/county/point reproduction.

GNIS point data do not supply the displayed terrain or corridors. Both frames use explicitly synthetic relief gaussians and generalized context lines; the Lake Superior row stores a mid-lake reference point and draws no shoreline.

State frames are rectangles, not state-boundary clipping masks. Both rectangles include areas outside their state outlines (including Canadian waters of the Great Lakes); no boundary geometry is claimed.
